newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH confident in case against Guinness.
newsitem.headline: LVMH confident in case against Guinness.

text.p: Luxury goods group LVMH is confident it will prevail in an arbitration proceeding that it requested on Friday to settle a dispute with drinks group Guinness Plc, a source at the French company said.

At issue is whether LVMH has the right to buy Guinness's stakes in their joint distribution ventures and in champagne and spirits group Moet Hennessy if Guinness goes ahead with its planned merger with Grand Metropolitan Plc.
The holdings, and most importantly, the 10 joint distribution ventures in France, the United States and key far eastern markets, are seen as crucial to the success of the Guinness-Grand Met alliance.

LVMH, Guinness's largest shareholder with 14 percent, opposes the merger and is pressing Guinness to split its spirits and brewing operations instead and merge the spirits business with LVMH's to create a global drinks leader.
LVMH said on May 28 that the proposed Guinness-Grand Met merger constituted a "control event" through a change in the ownership of Guinness that brought a rival into the picture.

As a result, it said it had the right under a 1994 accord to exercise options to buy Guinness's holdings in Moet Hennessy and the distribution ventures for a value estimated by analysts at roughly 10 billion francs.
Guinness says LVMH's claim lacks any legal basis and expressed confidence on Friday that the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) would agree.

But the LVMH source who spoke on condition of anonymity said law professor Alain Viandier, a specialist in French commercial law, had concluded that the Guinness-Grand Met merger did represent a "control event."

LVMH officials have said that, although Guinness appears to be taking control, Grand Met would account for just over 52 percent of the new merged group's capital and Grand Met managers would hold a majority of the key positions.
The company source said the ICC arbitration would be held in Paris.
